title: Dogs were widely distributed across western Eurasia during the Palaeolithic
version: Nature 651, 995–1003, DOI 10.1038/s41586-026-10170-x. UCL version-of-record PDF; author list abbreviated.
lineage: Primary direct specimen dates and nuclear genomes from Pınarbaşı and Gough’s Cave, distinct from the Bonn-Oberkassel material.

passages.locator: pp. 996–997, Dogs were widespread during the Palaeolithic; Fig. 1
passages.note: Identifies directly dated canids from Pınarbaşı and Gough’s Cave as dogs using nuclear DNA. The paper provides specimen-specific calibrated ranges.
